name: What if my garage is too close to the property line?

mainEntity.name: Can a garage conversion still be approved if the structure is very close to a side or rear property line in Glendale or Pasadena?
mainEntity.text: Can a garage conversion still be approved if the structure is very close to a side or rear property line in Glendale or Pasadena?

acceptedAnswer.text: Garage-to-ADU projects often succeed on tight urban lots, but property line proximity adds complexity. The city may require fire-rated exterior walls, limited openings, or other construction details depending on how close the structure sits to the boundary. If the garage already violates current expectations, the conversion may still be possible, but the design could need added protection, modified windows, or changes to roof overhangs and access points. Homeowners should not assume that an existing garage automatically qualifies just because it is already built. The approval depends on the current condition, local rules, and how the finished unit will meet safety and habitability standards. A contractor or designer should check the measured setbacks before promising a straightforward conversion. This is especially important in older neighborhoods where garages were built under different standards than today’s ADU requirements.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage near a property line can still sometimes be converted, but proximity to the boundary may affect wall rating, openings, setbacks, and fire separation requirements. The existing structure’s location is one of the first things to verify before design work starts.
